{{DISPLAYTITLE:AI Feynman}}
'''AI Feynman: Physics-Inspired Symmetry & Dimensional Symbolic Discovery'''
[[Category:Principia Machina]] [[Category:Tools]]

== Overview & Architectural Fit ==
Developed by Udrescu & Tegmark (MIT), '''AI Feynman''' is a symbolic regression framework designed specifically around the fundamental structural properties of theoretical physics: dimensional homogeneity, translational/rotational symmetries, separable sub-functions, and polynomial invariants.

== Mathematical Evaluation for TPM & SVD ==
* '''Noether Symmetry Exploitation (9.0/10):''' Unlike blind genetic algorithms, AI Feynman tests datasets for fundamental physical symmetries (e.g., <math>f(x, y) = g(x + y)</math> or <math>f(x, y) = g(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2})</math>). This directly mirrors Noether's First Theorem: identified symmetries correspond to underlying continuous conservation laws.
* '''Dimensional Analysis (Buckingham <math>\Pi</math> Theorem):''' Enforces strict physical units, reducing the dimensional search space prior to expression generation.
* '''NN-Driven Recursive Graph Decomposition:''' Uses trained neural networks as surrogates to inspect partial derivatives and split complex multi-variable field dynamics into simpler, separable lower-dimensional algebraic trees.

== Strategic Role in SVD ==
AI Feynman serves as the primary automated tool within TPM for verifying whether empirical field data exhibits the precise Maxwellian symmetries required by Structured Vacuum Dynamics (SVD).
